paras: The killing of Remus White was the shooting of a Black man accused of taking part in the murder of Jesse Baldwin by a deputy sheriff who was arresting him in Conecuh County, Alabama, in July 1910. His death surfaced in the press only weeks later, as an aside in reports on the capture of another suspect and on a mob's attempt on the Evergreen jail. The reports differ on his first name, the deputy's name and the timing.

Jesse Baldwin, an aged farmer who lived alone near Wilcox Station, was found near the back door of his home with his skull crushed by a blow from a hoe; the Montgomery Advertiser dated the murder July 7. He was said to have kept large sums of money at home, and the money was missing. Over the following month Conecuh County officers pursued and arrested several Black suspects.

According to an Evergreen special to the Montgomery Advertiser on August 4, White had been "killed a few days after the tragedy by a shot fired by Deputy Sheriff Nalls." A later Evergreen report in the same paper called him "the third negro" accused in the murder and said he was shot and killed by a deputy sheriff "who was in the act of arresting him." Neither account says where the shooting took place, what led the deputy to fire, or whether White resisted.

Albert Johnson, captured in lower Escambia County on August 4, was said to have named White as the man who struck the fatal blow. At Mobile on August 7, Johnson told a reporter that John Manuel had used a club and White the hoe while he only looked on, and Manuel called him a liar. Sheriff Irwin said he would not be surprised if Johnson told the truth.

In the meantime, a mob of about 100 armed men surrounded the Conecuh County jail at Evergreen on the night of August 6 and dispersed when Company K of the Alabama National Guard formed a line around it. Johnson and Manuel were then taken to the Mobile jail for safekeeping. No report of an inquest into White's death or of any inquiry into the shooting appears in the coverage.

White's death appeared only as a single sentence inside the Montgomery Advertiser's stories on the Baldwin case, under headlines such as "Chase for Negro Ends" and "Rush Negroes from Conecuh." The paper named no source for its account of the shooting and presented White's part in the murder through Johnson's statement, "it is claimed." The Birmingham Age-Herald reported Johnson's capture without naming White.

The Richmond Planet, a Black weekly, reprinted the Mobile dispatch on August 13 as "Negro Confessed to the Murder," naming "Remas White" as the man with the hoe but omitting the clause about his killing. Beside it the Planet ran "By the Soldiers," a brief on the attack on the Evergreen jail checked by troops.

The August 4 Evergreen report named the dead man Thomas White and the deputy Nalls, while the Mobile dispatch printed August 8 gave Remus White and Deputy Sheriff Noel. A Deputy Sheriff H. F. Nalls of Conecuh County appears in the August 7 report on the jail mob, which lends support to the name Nalls. The timing is given as "a few days after the tragedy," "several days ago" and "three weeks ago" as of August 7; with the murder dated July 7, the first and last place the shooting in mid-July.

reader.title: Killing of Remus White
bases: White was shot and killed by a deputy sheriff in the act of arresting him, with no crowd reported (A1, A4).
Only the Montgomery Advertiser reports the killing, in two dispatches from its Evergreen and Mobile correspondents (A1, A4); the Richmond Planet's reprint names White only as accused (A9).

accounts.label: Evergreen correspondent, Aug 4
accounts.gist: Johnson was said to have stated that Thomas White struck the fatal hoe blow; White had been killed a few days after the murder by a shot fired by Deputy Sheriff Nalls.

accounts.label: Evergreen correspondent, Aug 7
accounts.gist: Remus White, the third man accused in the murder, was shot and killed several days earlier by a deputy sheriff in the act of arresting him.

accounts.label: Mobile dispatch (Johnson's statement)
accounts.gist: Johnson said Remus White had the hoe; the white version adds that White was killed by Deputy Sheriff Noel three weeks before, which the Planet's reprint omits.

framing.detail: The Montgomery Advertiser mentioned the shooting in a single sentence inside stories headed 'Chase for Negro Ends' and 'Rush Negroes from Conecuh', giving no source or circumstances.
The Richmond Planet ran the Mobile dispatch as 'Negro Confessed to the Murder', naming 'Remas White' but not his killing.

conflicts.note: Remas is likely an OCR or typesetting variant of Remus; Thomas appears only in the first report.
A Conecuh deputy named H. F. Nalls appears in A3, which supports Nalls; the Noel version comes from a Mobile dispatch.

versions.value: a few days after the murder (murder July 7)

conflicts.note: The Mobile 'three weeks' fits the Aug 4 Evergreen report; 'several days ago' in the Aug 7 Evergreen report may be loose wording.
